claims.text: Combining high-throughput calorimetry with machine learning can determine HEA melting temperatures.
The combined approach can determine HEA enthalpies of fusion.
The combined approach can determine HEA entropies of fusion.
The combined approach can determine HEA volume changes at melting.
The combined approach can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of HEAs.
The combined calorimetry and machine-learning approach is efficient.
High-throughput calorimetry directly measures the relevant thermodynamic properties.
Machine-learning models can capture complex nonlinear relationships among HEA composition, structure, and thermodynamic properties.
Learning composition–structure–property relationships enables predictions for unexplored HEA compositions.
Atomic-size mismatch, mixing entropy, and valence-electron concentration mediate the relationship between HEA composition and thermodynamic properties.
The approach will predict each listed thermodynamic property within ±5% of experimental benchmarks.
The ±5% performance will apply across a wide range of HEA compositions.
Traditional experimental methods for determining these thermodynamic properties are time-consuming.
Traditional experimental methods have limited compositional coverage.
The approach is applicable to HEAs having well-characterized compositional and structural descriptors.
The approach may be less effective for alloys with extreme compositional or structural heterogeneity.
Machine-learning prediction accuracy depends on the quality and diversity of the training dataset.
The approach may perform poorly for compositions far outside the training-data range.
Controlled atmospheric conditions prevent oxidation or contamination during the experiments.
A sufficiently diverse HEA dataset is required to train the proposed models successfully.
